lines.japanese: 「おったまげた」
lines.english: “Well, knock me sideways.”

lines.japanese: 俺は芸術家らしく、自分の感情を卍型のボディランゲージで表現した。
lines.english: Like a true artist, I expressed my emotions through body language, twisting my limbs into a human pinwheel.

lines.japanese: 「シーット」
lines.english: “Shiiit.”

lines.japanese: それに対して浅黒い肌の芸術家は、無表情で感想を述べた。
lines.english: In reply, the dark-skinned artist delivered his critique without expression.

lines.japanese: 「やあおはよう、クロードくん。元気？」
lines.english: “Good morning, Claude. How've you been?”

lines.japanese: 「ウザいなおまえ。おはよう」
lines.english: “God, you're annoying. Morning.”

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードは鞄からミネラルウォーターの入ったペットボトルを取り出すと、ぐいと喉に流しこんだ。
lines.english: Haryu Claude drew a bottle of mineral water from his bag and poured it down his throat.

lines.japanese: 周囲の生徒たちが、努めて俺たちを空気のように扱っているのが伝わってくる。傍からは不穏な関係にでも見えるんだろうか。
lines.english: I could feel every student around us making a concerted effort to treat us as empty air. Perhaps the relationship looked ominous from outside.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、クロードくんが来てくれて羽田嬉しいぞう。これで今日から羽田班が本格的に活動できる。今日からシクヨロ」
lines.english: “Claude, old boy, Haneda is delighted you came. Now the Haneda Squad can commence serious operations. Let’s do this, Claude!”

lines.japanese: 「へえへえ」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: ほほう、意外にも肯定的な答えが返ってきた。羽田班としての活動に協力してくれるというのか。
lines.english: Well, well. An unexpectedly affirmative answer. Did he mean to cooperate with the Haneda Squad?

lines.japanese: といっても製作班が全員揃うことはありがたいが、ハリュー・クロードはこの学園で危険人物度Ｓランクの超危険人物だ。
lines.english: Having every member of the production team present was welcome. That said, Haryu Claude was an S-rank threat—the most dangerous kind of student in the whole academy.

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香と違い、隼人や鷹志の存在を知っていて、尚且つ伽楼羅にまで会っている。俺は充分に警戒しつつ、ハリュー・クロードの目の動きを追った。
lines.english: Unlike Asuka Watarai, he knew both Hayato and Takashi existed, and had even met Karura. Keeping my guard firmly raised, I tracked Haryu Claude's eyes.

lines.japanese: その視線の先はいつものように空間の中を回遊している。なにか聞いてくるかと思ったけど、目の前の俺を認識してるのか分からないくらい一箇所に落ちつかない。
lines.english: As always, his gaze went cruising through space. I expected him to ask something, but his eyes never rested anywhere long enough for me to tell whether he even recognized the person before him.

lines.japanese: 「俺の地道な感化活動が功を奏して、クロードくんの出席に繋がったとこういうわけか」
lines.english: “So my patient campaign of influence has borne fruit and brought Claude back to school.”

lines.japanese: 「あんたと俺が会うのはこれで二回目でしょオ」
lines.english: “This is only the second time you and I have met, riiight?”

lines.japanese: 「くくくクロードさん、お声が大きゅうございますっ！」
lines.english: “M-Mr. Claude, you’re speaking rather loudly!”

lines.japanese: 俺は慌てて口を押さえようとしたが、鬱陶しげに右手で払われた。ちっ、シャレの通じないやつ。
lines.english: I hurried to cover his mouth, but he brushed me away with an irritated right hand. Tch. The man couldn't take a joke.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあなんだ、今日はフツーに学校来ただけか？」
lines.english: “So what, you just came to school like normal today?”

lines.japanese: 「いやァ、もう面倒くせえから来月まで瀬戸内海に行って全島制覇でもしようかと思ってたんだがなァ」
lines.english: “Nah. I got sick of everything and thought I’d spend the rest of the month island-hopping around the Seto Inland Sea, conquering every last one.”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ、面白そうだな。俺も誘ってくれよ、旅費付きで」
lines.english: “Oh, that sounds fun. Invite me along, all expenses paid.”

lines.japanese: 「切符を買いに駅まで行ったところで明日香に出くわしてなァ、学校に来いって呼びだされた」
lines.english: “Got as far as the station to buy a ticket, then ran into Asuka. She summoned me to school.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　呼びだされたって……いや、あんたいつもならビッチビッチ言いながら蹴り入れて、そんな召集なんか聞く耳持たないだろう」
lines.english: “Hm? Summoned...? Normally you'd call her a bitch, kick her, and refuse to hear a word of it.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ？　さては針生蔵人、あの女に弱味でも握られてるのか？　なんつって、心臓に剛毛生えまくりのハリュー・クロードに限って、弱みなんかあるわけ──」
lines.english: “Heh heh. Don't tell me, Claude—does that woman have something on you? No, surely not. Haryu Claude has steel wool growing on his heart. A man like you couldn't possibly have a weakness—”

lines.japanese: 「古い付き合いでなァ、色々と若気のいたりを見られてるんだよ」
lines.english: “We go back a long way. She saw plenty of the stupid shit I did when I was young.”

lines.japanese: 「ひ、ひええ、ほんとに握られてたのか……あのハリュー・クロードすら脅迫するとは、あな恐ろしい女だ。なあなあ、暗殺しちゃえば？」
lines.english: “Y-you mean she really does have something on you...? To think even Haryu Claude could be blackmailed. What a terrifying woman. Hey, why not assassinate her?”

lines.japanese: 「フツーのやつならそうしてっけど、いい加減付き合い長ぇからなァ。ま、その分こっちも利用出来るときはさせてもらってっから、別にいいでしょ」
lines.english: “If she were anybody else, I would. But we've known each other too damn long. And I make use of her whenever she's useful, so it's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、仲いいなあんたら。で、弱点ってなんだ。靴下のかかとに穴でも開いてたのか」
lines.english: “Man, you two are close. So what’s this weakness? A hole in the heel of your sock or something?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、俺もガキの時分には、人並みに恋愛の詞とか書いてたからなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. When I was a brat, even I wrote love lyrics like any ordinary boy.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそれは恥ずかしいなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, that *is* embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、先輩とぱね田くん。おはよー、仲よさそうだね」
lines.english: “Oh, Claude and Paneda. Morning. You two look cozy.”

lines.japanese: 「ファーック」
lines.english: “Fuuuck.”

lines.japanese: 「ビーッチ」
lines.english: “Biiitch.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちの微笑ましい朝の挨拶に、クラスメイトたちは誰一人混ざってこようとはしなかった。
lines.english: Not one of our classmates attempted to join our heartwarming morning greeting.

lines.japanese: 「火曜の放課後、よく集まってくれた我が至嘱の精鋭たちよ！」
lines.english: “And so, on this Tuesday after school, you have assembled at last, my most trusted elites!”

lines.japanese: 精鋭たちはどいつもこいつもしらけ切った顔だ。やる気のほどが窺える。
lines.english: Every last elite wore an expression of utter indifference. Their enthusiasm shone through.

lines.japanese: 「甘ったれるなこの腑抜けども！」
lines.english: “Quit coddling yourselves, you spineless fools!”

lines.japanese: 俺は前言を撤回した。リーダーとは己の間違いであろうと認められる器を持っていなければならない。
lines.english: I retracted my previous statement. A leader must possess the greatness of spirit to acknowledge even his own mistakes.

lines.japanese: 「えー、我々はメンバーが中々揃わなかったこともあり、出足からして遅れております。これを取りもどすためには大車輪の働きを期待されるわけだが、その辺どう思うよ渡良瀬橋さん」
lines.english: “Now, our difficulty assembling the members has left us behind from the very start. Catching up will require prodigious labor. Your thoughts, Miss Watarase Bridge?”

lines.japanese: 「パパイアくんに人望がないよね」
lines.english: “Papaya has no charisma.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは分かっている、今はこれから先どうするかを論じておる。はい、クロード」
lines.english: “I know that already. We are discussing what to do from this point forward. Claude?”

lines.japanese: 「ぱね田に人望がねえんじゃねえのォ？」
lines.english: “Maybe Paneda just has no charisma.”

lines.japanese: 「き、貴様までぱね田って言うな！　もういい、山科教えてくれ、俺たちはどうすればいい」
lines.english: “D-don't you start calling me Paneda! Enough. Yamashina, tell me what we should do.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君に任せるよ」
lines.english: “I'll leave it to you, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶふぉっ！」
lines.english: “Bffft!”

lines.japanese: 「な、なに？　どしたのパナマ運河くん」
lines.english: “Wh-what? What's wrong, Panama Canal?”

lines.japanese: 「す、すまん。つい任せるという言葉の秘められた魔力に中てられてしまった」
lines.english: “S-sorry. The occult power concealed within the words 'leave it to you' struck me full force.”

lines.japanese: つまり狩男病だ。
lines.english: In other words, a case of Karuo disease.

lines.japanese: 「オチくらい付けろよつまんねえヤツだなあ」
lines.english: “At least give the joke a punch line. You're one boring bastard.”

lines.japanese: そして山科京もあんたにだけは言われたくないと思う。
lines.english: And I was pretty sure Miyako Yamashina was thinking, *You’re one to talk.*

lines.japanese: 「役割分担する？」
lines.english: “Should we divide up the work?”

lines.japanese: 山科の首の角度がクロードの対面に座る渡来に向けてがっちりと固定された。クロードが山科の後頭部を見つめつつ、眼鏡をくいとあげた。
lines.english: Miyako fixed her gaze firmly on Watarai, who sat opposite Claude. Claude stared at the back of Miyako's head and pushed up his glasses.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだね、じゃあそろそろ始めよっか！」
lines.english: “Y-yes, good idea. Let's get started!”

lines.japanese: 何故か俺が気を使う羽目になった。くそ、まるで班長みたいじゃないか。
lines.english: Somehow I was the one forced to smooth things over. Damn it, I was practically acting like the group leader.

lines.japanese: 「と言ってもたかが文集だからな。四人でやればそんなに時間がかかる量でもないはずだ」
lines.english: “It's only a class anthology, after all. With four of us, it shouldn't take terribly long.”

lines.japanese: 「というわけで、まずは文集をまとめて出席番号順に重ねるところから始めるか。この仕事は力もいらないし、たった一人しかいない、か弱い女の子の山科に任せてもいいかな」
lines.english: “So first, let's collate the compositions and stack them in student-number order. It requires no strength, so may I entrust it to Yamashina, the one and only delicate girl among us?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “The hell you say.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、分かりました」
lines.english: “Yes, understood.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “The hell you say.”

lines.japanese: 「クロードにはクラス写真のレイアウトを頼む。全員が必ず一枚は入るカンジで。あとは趣味に走って構わん」
lines.english: “Claude, you handle the layout for the class photos. Make sure everybody appears at least once. Beyond that, indulge your tastes.”

lines.japanese: 「へェ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来、おまえは割り箸を鼻の穴に突っこみ、もう片方を手に握って昇降口に行ってくれ。誰かに会ったら『私の割り箸片方知りませんか？』と聞くんだぞ」
lines.english: “Watarai, insert one disposable chopstick into a nostril, hold its mate in your hand, and go stand by the school entrance. Whenever you meet someone, ask, 'Have you seen my other chopstick?'”

lines.japanese: 「山科ー、私男子の分やるから、そっちの作文ちょうだい」
lines.english: “Yamashina, I'll take the boys' half. Pass me those compositions.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだおまえ、芸人のくせにヨゴレなんか出来ないとでも言うのか。くそ、渡来とは上手くやっていけそうだと思っていたのにがっかりだぜ」
lines.english: “What, you think a professional comedian is above humiliating herself? Damn it, and I thought you and I might work well together.”

lines.japanese: しかし渡来は山科と二人で入学式のことなんかを話しはじめた。最初に仲がよかったＤ子がどうとかお互いの第一印象がどうとか、くそ普通の女の子みたいな真似をしやがって。輝いてるじゃないか。
lines.english: But Watarai started talking with Yamashina about the entrance ceremony: Girl D, her first friend, what they had first thought of each other, and other such things. Damn her, acting like an ordinary girl. She was positively radiant.

lines.japanese: 「さてじゃあ、俺も仕事しに行くか」
lines.english: “Well, guess I'll get to work too.”

lines.japanese: 俺は財布を片手に立ちあがった。
lines.english: Wallet in hand, I rose.

lines.japanese: 「ん、どしたの出かける準備なんか始めて」
lines.english: “Hm? What’re you getting ready to go out for?”

lines.japanese: 「初日は班長様が飲み物でも買ってきてやろう」
lines.english: “On our first day, your gracious group leader will buy everybody drinks.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、意外と優しいじゃん班長」
lines.english: “Huh. You're surprisingly nice, Chief.”

lines.japanese: 「ホントだ、頼りになるね班長」
lines.english: “You really are dependable, Chief.”

lines.japanese: 「へェ、そりゃ悪いな班長」
lines.english: “Well, that's mighty kind of you, Chief.”

lines.japanese: 現金な連中だ。だが俺は広い心で受けとめた。
lines.english: What a mercenary bunch. But I embraced them with a generous heart.

lines.japanese: 「よーし何がいい。遠慮せずに言ってみなさい」
lines.english: “All right, what would everybody like? Don't be shy.”

lines.japanese: 「私はアップルジュースがいいなー」
lines.english: “Apple juice for me.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ私、マテ茶」
lines.english: “Then I’ll have maté.”

lines.japanese: 「俺、黒酢」
lines.english: “Black vinegar.”

lines.japanese: 「せめてコンビニに置いてあるものにしてください」
lines.english: “Please ask for something the convenience store might conceivably carry.”

lines.japanese: ま、いいや。適当に買ってこよう。どうせこの連中タダなら何でも飲むだろ。
lines.english: Oh, well. I would buy something at random. These people would drink anything if it was free.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ぱね田くん一人じゃ大変でしょ。私も行くよ」
lines.english: “Oh, carrying it alone will be hard, Paneda. I'll come too.”

lines.japanese: 「おっ？」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: ほほう、いい心がけだ。渡来にしては使えるじゃないか。
lines.english: Well, well. An admirable impulse. Watarai could be useful after all.

lines.japanese: 「ふふん、渡来も誰が実力者か分かってきたじゃないか。いいだろう、褒美としてお菓子選択の権限はおまえに……」
lines.english: “Hmph. So Watarai has finally begun to grasp who holds the real power. Very well. As your reward, you may choose the snacks—”

lines.japanese: 「私、行こうか？」
lines.english: “Shall I go?”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　え、なに山科も……」
lines.english: “Huh? What, you too, Yamashina...?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なんだったら俺が付きあってやるよ」
lines.english: “Hell, I'll come with you if you like.”

lines.japanese: 「えええっ！？」
lines.english: “Whaaat!?”

lines.japanese: な、なんの罠だ。なんで俺がこんなに大人気なんだ。
lines.english: Wh-what trap was this? Why was I suddenly so popular?

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Y-yeah. Thanks.”

lines.japanese: あまりに想定外、というか初めての体験に思わず素でお礼を言ってしまった。くそ、どうせこいつらお菓子を選びたいとかそんな理由だってのに。
lines.english: It was so unexpected—indeed, so unprecedented—that I thanked them sincerely without thinking. Damn it. They only wanted to choose the snacks themselves.

lines.japanese: 「え、と……じゃあ始めたばっかりの手を止めるのもなんだしな……」
lines.english: “Um... But you've only just started working. It would be a shame to stop...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ渡来、一番男くさいおまえに頼もう」
lines.english: “Watarai, I'll entrust it to you. You're the manliest one here.”

lines.japanese: 「私がいいんだ」
lines.english: “You want *me*?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだその言い方は。単に最初に言ったからとか、そんなんだ」
lines.english: “Wh-what kind of way is that to say it? You only asked first. That's all.”

lines.japanese: 「よし」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「ぐっ、コノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Ghk. You little...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ行くぞぱね田ー、付いてこーい」
lines.english: “Come along, Paneda. Keep up!”

lines.japanese: 「お、おまえが仕切るなあっ！」
lines.english: “D-don’t start bossing me around!”

lines.japanese: 何故か俺が渡来を追いかける形になった。くそ、あの女には誰が上位者であるか、きちんと躾けてやらなくては……。
lines.english: Somehow I ended up following Watarai. Damn that woman. I would have to teach her exactly which of us outranked the other...

lines.japanese: くくくあの女今に見てろよ、ひいひい言わせてやるぜ。
lines.english: Heh heh heh. Just you wait. I'll have you crying for mercy.

lines.japanese: 「ぱね田くーん、遅いよー」
lines.english: “Paneda! You're too slow!”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！」
lines.english: “Coming!”

lines.japanese: 「ひいっ、ひいっ……」
lines.english: “Huff... huff...”

lines.japanese: 手を後ろに組みながら歩く渡来の隣で、何故か俺は両手に荷物をぶら下げていた。
lines.english: For some reason, I walked beside Watarai with bags hanging from both hands while she strolled with hers clasped behind her back.

lines.japanese: ひとの金だと思って、２リットルのペットボトルを人数分買いやがった。その他お菓子もろもろ。
lines.english: Since it wasn't her money, she had bought one two-liter bottle per person. Plus snacks of every description.

lines.japanese: 「くっ、階段くらい持ってくれてもいいじゃないか」
lines.english: “Ngh. You could at least carry some of this up the stairs.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君ならきっと全部持ってくれるよね」
lines.english: “Haneda would carry all of it for me. I'm sure of that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来は俺の方へ顔も向けずに言った。おかしい、俺の予定ではこいつの腰のリボンにビニール袋をくくりつけて歩かせる予定だったんだが……。
lines.english: Watarai said it without even turning toward me. Strange. My plan had been to tie the bags to the ribbon at her waist and make *her* carry them...

lines.japanese: 「誰だってこんな仕打ちを受けたら、下り階段に差しかかったあたりでドロップキックを食らわすと思うぞ」
lines.english: “Anybody subjected to this treatment would drop-kick you down the stairs the moment we reached them.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか羽田君なら弱音なんて吐かないか」
lines.english: “Then again, Haneda would never whine about something like this.”

lines.japanese: 「聞けよ。聞いてよ俺の話。おまえがなにを期待してるのか知らないけど、俺こそが羽田」
lines.english: “Listen to me. Hear what I'm saying. I don't know what you expect, but *I* am Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「私の知ってる羽田君じゃないなあ」
lines.english: “You're not the Haneda I know.”

lines.japanese: 「ええい、うるさい。なんなんだおまえは。俺の恋人か」
lines.english: “Oh, shut up. What are you, my girlfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そういうことになってるけど」
lines.english: “Yes. Officially, anyway.”

lines.japanese: 俺は聞こえやすいように渡来の耳元で舌打ちを無数に繰りかえした。
lines.english: I leaned close to Watarai's ear and clicked my tongue at her over and over, making certain she heard every one.

lines.japanese: 「くそう、おまえそんなにハネダタカシが好きか」
lines.english: “Damn it. Do you love Takashi Haneda that much?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、どうだろう？　私、羽田君と話したことほとんどないんだよね」
lines.english: “Who knows? I've hardly ever spoken to Haneda.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 見当違いの発言に、思わず俺は足を止めた。
lines.english: Her wildly misplaced remark stopped me in my tracks.

lines.japanese: 「話したことないっつうか」
lines.english: “It's less that you haven't spoken to him...”

lines.japanese: 話しかけられなかったのはこっちなんだが。
lines.english: I was the one who had never managed to speak to her.

lines.japanese: 「さっきも羽田君なら私と一緒に行こうなんて言わないと思うんだよ」
lines.english: “I don't think Haneda would have asked me to come along just now, either.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「はああ？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 二、三歩進んで渡来が足を止めて振りかえった。俺が付いてこないのに気がついたんだろう。
lines.english: Watarai took another two or three steps, then stopped and looked back. She must have noticed I was no longer following.

lines.japanese: この女なにか勘違いしてないか。言わないっていうか、そもそもこんな機会が来ること自体ありえなかったのに。
lines.english: Was this woman misunderstanding something? It wasn't that he wouldn't have asked her. The opportunity itself could never have existed in the first place.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあおまえ、羽田君から誘われたらどうすんの」
lines.english: “Then what would you do if Haneda invited you?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: えっ、うそ。なんでこのひと顔赤らめて目線そらしてんの。
lines.english: Wait. No. Why was she blushing and looking away?

lines.japanese: 「でもぱね田くんに誘われても嬉しくもなんともないよね」
lines.english: “But I wouldn't be the least bit happy if Paneda invited me.”

lines.japanese: だけどすぐに元の顔に戻った。ふてぶてしいやつだ。
lines.english: She promptly returned to her usual expression. What a brazen creature.

lines.japanese: 「うるさい駄姫。とっとと戻るぞ」
lines.english: “Shut up, Princess Failure. Let's get back.”

lines.japanese: 俺は先陣をきって歩きはじめた。
lines.english: I took the lead and resumed walking.

lines.japanese: それにしてもさすがはプリンセス、さっきの顔はヤバかった。危うく惚れるかと思ったぜ。
lines.english: Still, she was a princess. That face just now had been lethal. I had very nearly fallen for her.

lines.japanese: もくもく。
lines.english: And on we worked, in silence.

lines.japanese: もくもく。
lines.english: And on we worked, in silence.

lines.japanese: 辞書をぱらぱらとめくりながら考えた。
lines.english: I thought as I idly riffled through a dictionary.

lines.japanese: こいつらよく何もしゃべらないまま延々と続けられるな。
lines.english: How could these people keep going forever without saying a word?

lines.japanese: クロードも山科もほとんど微動だにしないまま作業を続けている。いや、確かに俺も作業中は集中してやりたいし、話しながら手を動かせる器用なタイプでもない。
lines.english: Claude and Yamashina kept working, barely shifting in their seats. Granted, I preferred to concentrate while I worked too, and I wasn't deft enough to keep my hands moving while I talked.

lines.japanese: だがもう二時間だぞ。二時間一言も話さず、休憩もとらずに作業を黙々と続けていた。たまにジュースやお菓子を手に取るのみで、事務的会話もほとんどない。
lines.english: But it had been two hours. Two hours of silent labor without a break. Apart from occasionally reaching for juice or a snack, they had exchanged scarcely even a practical word.

lines.japanese: 俺はわざとらしく腕を天井に向けて伸ばし、背もたれに寄りかかった。
lines.english: With theatrical exaggeration, I stretched both arms toward the ceiling and leaned back in my chair.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、つっかれったな～」
lines.english: “Aaaah, I am exhauuusted.”

lines.japanese: んっ、と伸びをして肩の位置をコキンと上下させる俺。ついでに左右の捻りも加えてみた。
lines.english: I stretched with a grunt, hunching and dropping my shoulders until one cracked. For good measure, I twisted from side to side.

lines.japanese: しかし非協力的な班員たちからの返事はなかった。くそう、こうなったら意地でも気になるようなことを言ってやる。
lines.english: But my uncooperative teammates offered no response. Damn it. I would say something so intriguing they couldn't possibly ignore it.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、アサガオだったのかあ」
lines.english: “Ohhh. So it was a morning glory.”

lines.japanese: だ、ダメなのか。俺は自信を失いかけ、連中に見えぬよう人知れず泣いた。
lines.english: N-no good? My confidence began to falter, and I wept in secret where they couldn't see.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh. That reminds me.”

lines.japanese: 「んっ」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: なにが違うんだろう……納得いかないが、とりあえず会話が出来そうなのでハリュー・クロードの話に耳を傾けることにした。
lines.english: What was the difference...? I couldn't accept this, but conversation now seemed possible, so I decided to hear Haryu Claude out.

lines.japanese: 「俺、冬休みの間は喜望峰から入って、ンジャメナまで行こうと思ってたんだ。なァ明日香、その間の新聞とっといてくんねェかな」
lines.english: “Over winter break, I was thinking of starting at the Cape of Good Hope and making my way to N'Djamena. Hey, Asuka, save the newspapers for me while I'm gone, would ya?”

lines.japanese: あまり日常では耳にしない地名が聞こえたが、そこにツッコミは入れなかった。
lines.english: Those were not place names one often heard in ordinary conversation, but I declined to comment.

lines.japanese: 「先輩、今度はアフリカ？　好きだねえ」
lines.english: “Africa this time, Claude? You really do love it.”

lines.japanese: 「まァな……こふ、こふっ……で、どうなの。やってくれんのくれないの」
lines.english: “Suppose so... Cough, cough... So? Will you do it or not?”

lines.japanese: ハリューは話の途中でミネラルウォーターをあおった。冬だから喉が渇くみたいだ。
lines.english: Haryu took a swig of mineral water in mid-sentence. Apparently winter made his throat dry.

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、とっておくよ。でも途中が抜けてても文句言わないでね」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, I'll save them. Don't complain if there are gaps, though.”

lines.japanese: 「冬休みにアフリカか。どんだけ優雅なんだおまえ」
lines.english: “Africa over winter break? What kind of jet-setter are you?”

lines.japanese: 「でもアフリカには私も行きたい」
lines.english: “I'd like to go to Africa too.”

lines.japanese: 「卒業旅行に高内とでも行ってくれ」
lines.english: “Go with Takauchi for your graduation trip.”

lines.japanese: 「卒業旅行っていい響きだね。羽田君はどこかに行くの？」
lines.english: “Graduation trip has a lovely ring to it. Are you going anywhere, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、俺？」
lines.english: “What, me?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな卒業したら……旅行じゃないけど、遊園地にでも行こうかな」
lines.english: “Let's see. After graduation... It isn't exactly a trip, but maybe I'll go to an amusement park.”

lines.japanese: 思わぬところで俺に弾が飛んできた。いいぞ山科、その調子で返しやすい弾を投げてくれ。
lines.english: A conversational ball flew my way from an unexpected direction. Good, Yamashina. Keep tossing easy ones like that.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんと？」
lines.english: “With Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ山科、ぱね田くんには他に好きなひといるんだって。私とはホントに付きあってたわけじゃないから」
lines.english: “Oh, Yamashina, Paneda apparently likes somebody else. We were never really dating.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そうなの？　二年半も？」
lines.english: “What? For two and a half years?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「おい、いいのかバラして」
lines.english: “Hey, are you sure you should tell her?”

lines.japanese: 「山科は誰かにしゃべったりしないと思うよ」
lines.english: “I don't think Yamashina will tell anybody.”

lines.japanese: 「話す相手もいないからね」
lines.english: “I don't have anybody to tell.”

lines.japanese: 「そこのカラスは」
lines.english: “What about the crow over there?”

lines.japanese: 「先輩は最初から知ってる」
lines.english: “Claude knew from the beginning.”

lines.japanese: 「仮面恋人ご苦労さん。あと三ヶ月だ、適当にがんばれ」
lines.english: “Good work playing the sham lovers. Three months left. Half-ass it to the finish.”

lines.japanese: 「で、誰と行きたいって？」
lines.english: “So who did you want to go with?”

lines.japanese: 「いやらしい笑みを浮かべているおまえと違って、清らかな心を持った天使のような女の子だ。前から行きたいと言われてはいたんだが、俺は遊園地などという軟派な場所に行ったことがないからな」
lines.english: “An angelic girl with a pure heart, quite unlike you and your lecherous grin. She's been asking me for a while, but I've never visited anywhere as frivolous as an amusement park.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえも友達いねえもんなあ」
lines.english: “You really don't have any friends either.”

lines.japanese: 「ううううるさいっ！　なぜおまえが知っている！」
lines.english: “Sh-sh-shut up! How do you know that?”

lines.japanese: 「はぁ、コースターだのホラーハウスだの、臨死体験がしたけりゃあカナダで野生のグリズリーにメープルシロップでもぶっかけてきなよ。そっちの方がよっぽどエキサイティングでしょオ」
lines.english: “Roller coasters, haunted houses—if you want a near-death experience, go pour maple syrup on a wild grizzly in Canada. That'd be a hell of a lot more exciting.”

lines.japanese: 「黙れ。頼むから一人でアフリカライオンでもハンティングしててくれ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Please go hunt African lions by yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「だったらウイングランドなんてどう？　女の子なら喜ぶと思うよ」
lines.english: “Then how about Wingland? I think any girl would enjoy it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいよねあそこ。アトラクション以外でもパレードとか楽しめるし、キャラクターも人気あるしね」
lines.english: “Oh, that place is nice. The parade is fun even apart from the rides, and the characters are popular.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いやあそこは前に学校の遠足で行ったことあるらしい。初めての場所に連れていって驚かせてやりたいんだよ」
lines.english: “Well, she went there once on a school field trip. I want to take her somewhere new and surprise her.”

lines.japanese: 「いい歳して惚れた子の処女性にこだわるの、どうかと思うよ」
lines.english: “At your age, obsessing over whether the girl you love is untouched seems questionable.”

lines.japanese: 軽く希望を述べただけなのにどうしてここまで言われなくてはならないのだろう。俺はアップルジュースを紙コップに注いでチビチビと飲んだ。
lines.english: I had merely expressed a modest preference. Why did it warrant this? I poured apple juice into a paper cup and sipped it in tiny mouthfuls.

lines.japanese: 「それで先輩はホントに冬休みにアフリカ大陸に行くの？」
lines.english: “So, Claude, are you really going to Africa over winter break?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　まァ、そン時の気分次第だなァ。なんならご一緒いたしましょうか、ファッキン同級生。アフリカなんて行ったことないだろォ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Depends how I feel when the time comes. Should you so desire, I would be honored by your company, fucking classmate. Never been to Africa, have you?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、確かにこれからも行くことなんてなさそうだよね」
lines.english: “Hmm. True. I doubt I’ll ever go otherwise.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、それは面白そうだね。ちょっと距離が遠すぎるけど」
lines.english: “Hee hee. That does sound interesting. It's a little too far, though.”

lines.japanese: 「だねー、もっと近くなら行ってみたかったかな」
lines.english: “Yeah. If it were closer, I might have gone.”

lines.japanese: なにが違うんだろう……。
lines.english: What was the difference...?

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ後片付けは男組がやっておくから、先に帰ってていいぞ」
lines.english: “The guys will take care of cleanup. You two can head home.”

lines.japanese: 時間を見ると、いつもならアレキサンダーに入ってる時間。マスターに連絡を入れて、しばらくはアルバイトは休ませてもらおう。
lines.english: I checked the time. Ordinarily I would already be at Alexander. I would call the boss and ask for some time away from my shifts.

lines.japanese: 「さんくるー。じゃ、山科帰ろっか。どっか寄ってく？」
lines.english: “Thankies! Come on, Yamashina, let's go. Want to stop somewhere?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、渡来さんと一緒に帰るのも久しぶりだしね」
lines.english: “Sure. It has been a while since I walked home with you.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ駅前の『アーモンド』でも寄ってくか」
lines.english: “Then why don't we stop at Almond by the station?”

lines.japanese: 「待てや」
lines.english: “Hold it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は男の襟だけがっしとつかんで、女二人に手を振った。
lines.english: I caught Claude firmly by the collar and waved farewell to the two women.

lines.japanese: 「冗談だ、俺は羽田に話があるんだよ」
lines.english: “Kidding. I need to talk to Haneda.”

lines.japanese: なにが冗談なのか知らないが、ハリュー・クロードは俺が机を片付けている中、一人で椅子（無論他人の）に腰を下ろした。
lines.english: I had no idea which part was the joke, but while I cleared the desks, Haryu Claude sat alone in a chair—someone else's, naturally.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、一緒に遊びましょうとかそういう話か」
lines.english: “What is it? Are you going to ask me to play with you?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そんなとこだなァ」
lines.english: “Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そうなの！？」
lines.english: “Wait, really!?”

lines.japanese: クロードは相変わらず視線をふらふらとさ迷わせている。ひとと話すときは目ェ見ろ。
lines.english: As ever, Claude's gaze wandered aimlessly. Look a man in the eye when you speak to him.

lines.japanese: 「え、なにすんの。カラーボール野球とかかくれんぼとか？」
lines.english: “What'll we do? Color-ball baseball? Hide-and-seek?”

lines.japanese: 「ハハ、それもいいなあ。なんなら鬼ごっことか缶蹴りでもいいね」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Those sound good. Tag or kick-the-can would work too.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待て、おまえの場合、どこまで本気で言ってるのかワカラン」
lines.english: “Wait. With you, I can't tell how much of that is serious.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　俺？　冗談なんか一つも言ってねえけど」
lines.english: “Me? I haven't made a single joke.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうか、今朝会ったときに一つウソ言った。今日来たのに明日香関係なくってさァ、本当はニワトリから興味深い報告を受けて来たんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I did tell one lie when we met this morning. Coming here had nothing to do with Asuka. The truth is, Chicken gave me an interesting report, so I came to see for myself.”

lines.japanese: 「受けて来たんだって……え、マジで？」
lines.english: “You came because...? Wait, seriously?”

lines.japanese: げんなりした。カケルくんがこいつに話したのは明らかに嫌がらせだ。
lines.english: My spirits sank. Kakeru had told this man for the obvious purpose of tormenting me.

lines.japanese: 「ニワトリとは別に俺もしばらく観察させてもらうよ。よろしくな陛下、いや委員長か」
lines.english: “Chicken’s not the only one—I’ll be observing you for a while too. Looking forward to it, Your Majesty—or should I say Chairman?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえら、ひとを愛玩動物みたいに扱いおって……」
lines.english: “You people treat me like some kind of pet...”

lines.japanese: 「さっそくＨ組のやつ二人ほどのしたんだろ？　フフ、その調子で面白いもの見せてくれよ」
lines.english: “Already put down a couple boys from Class H, didn't you? Heh. Keep it up. Show me something interesting.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、うるさいうるさい。頭きた、おまえのガキの頃の恋愛詩探し出して毎日口ずさんでやる」
lines.english: “Oh, shut up, shut up. Now I'm angry. I'll hunt down the love lyrics you wrote as a kid and sing them every day.”

lines.japanese: 「ファック」
lines.english: “Fuck.”

lines.japanese: 品のない悪態をついていたが、ハリュー・クロードの口元はいつか見たかすかな笑いを浮かべていた。
lines.english: The curse lacked all refinement, but Haryu Claude's mouth bore that faint smile I had seen once before.

lines.japanese: 厄介の種が増えた。でも多分俺も目の前のやつと同じ笑いを浮かべていたと思う。自分じゃ分からないけど、そんな気がした。
lines.english: Another source of trouble had joined the fold. But I suspected I wore the same smile as the man before me. I couldn't see it myself, yet somehow I knew.
